Strascinati Dough

Puglian semolina pasta shaped by dragging each piece under the fingers.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

2 1/3 cups finely milled durum semolina
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp plus 1 tsp water
2/3 tsp fine salt
3 tbsp semolina for dusting

Preparation

1. Make a well in the semolina.

2. Dissolve the salt in the water.

3. Gradually pour the water into the center.

4. Draw in the semolina with a fork.

5. Knead by hand for 10 minutes.

6. Continue until smooth and elastic.

7. Cover.

8. Rest for 20 minutes.

9. Divide into several pieces.

10. Roll into ropes about 3/8 inch thick.

11. Cut into pieces about 1/2 inch long.

12. Place two or three fingertips on each piece.

13. Press and drag toward you to stretch and hollow the dough.

14. Lift each piece gently.

15. Arrange on a semolina-dusted tray.

16. Dry for 20–30 minutes.

17. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.

18. Cook for 6–7 minutes.

19. Drain.

Service

Serve with fried breadcrumbs and anchovies, tomato sauce, or another Puglian dressing.

Chef's note

Use even finger pressure to create a thinner center with slightly thicker edges.

Fileja Dough

Calabrian semolina pasta rolled around a thin metal rod.

Culurgiones Dough

Ogliastra pasta filled with potatoes, Pecorino, and mint and sealed in the traditional wheat-ear pattern.

Yield: about 6 servings

about 6 2/3 cups potatoes

1/4 cup finely chopped fresh mint

2/3 tsp fine salt

1. Boil the potatoes in their skins until completely tender.

2. Drain.

3. Peel while still hot.

4. Mash finely.

5. Cool completely.

6. Add the Pecorino, mint, garlic, olive oil, and salt.

7. Mix into a compact filling.

8. Cover and refrigerate.

9. Mix the durum flour and semolina.

18. Put about 1 tablespoon filling in the center.

19. Lift the edges of the disk.

20. Alternately pinch one side and then the other toward the center to create the traditional wheat-ear closure.

21. Seal the final point completely.

22. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.

23. Cook until the culurgiones rise to the surface, about 3–5 minutes.

24. Lift out with a slotted spoon.

Serve with simple tomato sauce and Pecorino or with olive oil and cheese.

The filling should be cold and compact before shaping or the wheat-ear seal becomes difficult to close.

Lorighittas Dough

Hand-braided Morgongiori pasta made with semolina, water, and salt.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

3 1/2 cups finely milled durum semolina
1 1/4 cups water
1/2 tsp fine salt
3 tbsp semolina for dusting

1. Dissolve the salt in the water.

2. Put the semolina in a large bowl.

3. Gradually add the water.

5. Transfer to a work surface.

7. Shape into a disk.

8. Cover in a closed container.

9. Rest for 10 minutes.

10. Pinch off small pieces.

11. Roll into thin strands about 8 inches long.

12. Wrap one strand twice around three fingers.

13. Join the ends firmly.

14. Slide the ring off your fingers.

15. Gently twist the two strands around one another to create the characteristic braid.

16. Arrange on a semolina-dusted towel.

Seal the ends before twisting the ring so the lorighittas do not open during cooking.

Fregola Dough

Traditional Sardinian durum-semola pasta formed by hand into tiny irregular balls and toasted.

Yield: about 3 cups dried fregola

Ingredients

3 cups medium or fine durum semolina
1 1/4 cups warm water
3/4 tsp fine salt
a generous pinch saffron, optional

Preparation

1. Dissolve the salt in the warm water.

2. Add the saffron if using and let it dissolve.

3. Put 1 tablespoon semolina in a scivedda or large shallow flat-bottomed bowl.

4. Add 1 tablespoon water.

5. Rub the semolina against the bottom with your fingertips and palm in continuous circular motions.

6. Once small clumps begin to form, add another small amount of semolina.

7. Add only a very small amount of water at a time.

8. Continue the circular motion, alternating semolina and water.

9. Stop when the balls reach about 1/16–1/8 inch.

10. Transfer formed balls to a parchment-lined baking sheet.

11. Continue until all semolina and water are used.

12. Air-dry for at least 1 hour; for a drier traditional result, leave until the next day.

13. Preheat the oven to 400°F.

14. Spread the fregola in a single layer.

15. Toast for 15–30 minutes, stirring halfway through.

16. Remove when dry and lightly golden.

17. Cool completely.

Service

Cook in broth or directly in a liquid sauce, risotto-style.

Chef's note

Adding the water by spoonfuls prevents the semolina from becoming one solid dough and lets separate irregular grains form.

Agnolotti Dough

Piedmont stuffed pasta filled with roast meat, mortadella, and Parmigiano.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

For the pasta
4 cups plus 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
2 large eggs
5 egg yolks
about 1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp water
3/4 tsp fine salt

For the filling
about 2/3 cup finely chopped mortadella
about 2 cups finely chopped lean roast pork, beef, chicken, or veal
2/3 cup finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano
1 large egg
scant 1/2 cup heavy cream
about 1 1/2 cups soft bread crumbs soaked in milk and squeezed dry
1/4 tsp ground nutmeg
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper
2/3 tsp fine salt

For serving
2/3 cup roast-pan juices
3 tbsp butter
1/3 cup finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano

Preparation

1. Grind the mortadella and roast meat very finely.

2. Grind them a second time.

3. Put the meats in a bowl.

4. Add the bread crumbs, Parmigiano, cream, and egg.

5. Add the salt, pepper, and nutmeg.

6. Mix into a compact filling.

7. Cover and refrigerate.

8. Make a well in the flour.

9. Add the 2 eggs, 5 yolks, and salt.

10. Add about 1/4 cup plus 1 tablespoon water first.

11. Knead.

12. Add the remaining water only if needed to produce a firm smooth dough.

13. Knead for 10–12 minutes.

14. Cover.

15. Rest for 30 minutes.

16. Roll the pasta thin, about 1/32–1/16 inch.

17. Cut into strips about 2 1/2 inches wide.

18. Place small portions of filling at regular intervals.

19. Fold the pasta over the filling.

20. Press out trapped air.

21. Seal firmly.

22. Cut with a fluted pastry wheel.

23. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.

24. Cook for 4–6 minutes, until the pasta is tender.

25. Drain gently.

Service

Layer with roast-pan juices, butter, and Parmigiano.

Chef's note

The pasta should be thin enough not to dominate the filling but sturdy enough to contain the rich stuffing.

Pizzoccheri Dough

Valtellina buckwheat pasta with potatoes, cabbage, Casera, grated cheese, and garlic butter.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

For the pizzoccheri
3 1/3 cups buckwheat flour
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp all-purpose flour
1 cup plus 2 tbsp warm water
3/4 tsp fine salt

For the dressing
about 3 1/3 cups potatoes
about 8 cups chopped savoy cabbage
about 1 2/3 cups thinly sliced Valtellina Casera
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano or Grana Padano
5 1/2 tbsp butter
3 garlic cloves
1 rosemary sprig, optional

Preparation

1. Mix the buckwheat flour and all-purpose flour.

2. Add the salt.

3. Gradually add the warm water.

4. Knead for about 5 minutes.

5. Continue until compact and uniform.

6. Cover.

7. Rest for 30 minutes.

8. Roll about 1/16–1/8 inch thick.

9. Cut bands 2 3/4–3 inches wide.

10. Stack the bands.

11. Cut into strips about 3/16 inch wide.

12. Peel the potatoes.

13. Cut into 1/2-inch cubes.

14. Cut the cabbage into pieces.

15. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.

16. Add the potatoes.

17. Cook for 5 minutes.

18. Add the cabbage and pizzoccheri.

19. Cook for about 10 minutes.

20. Meanwhile, thinly slice the Casera.

21. Melt the butter with the garlic and rosemary.

22. Let the garlic brown without burning.

23. Lift the pasta and vegetables out with a slotted spoon.

24. Arrange one layer in a warm serving dish.

25. Sprinkle with Casera and Parmigiano.

26. Continue layering.

27. Pour the hot flavored butter over the top.

Service

Serve immediately without excessive mixing.

Chef's note

Warm water helps the buckwheat starches bind and makes the dough easier to roll.

Casoncelli Dough

Bergamo stuffed pasta with a flour-and-semolina wrapper and a filling of meats, pear, Grana, amaretti, and spices.

Yield: about 12 servings

Ingredients

For the pasta
6 2/3 cups all-purpose flour
1 1/4 cups semolina

1 1/2 cups water
1 tsp fine salt

For the filling
about 2 cups fatty pork sausage meat
2 1/2 cups breadcrumbs
about 1 1/2 cups finely diced pear

2 large eggs

1 garlic clove
1/3 cup finely chopped parsley
1/4 tsp ground nutmeg
1/4 tsp ground cinnamon
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper
1 tsp fine salt
finely grated zest of 1/2 lemon

Preparation

1. Soak the raisins in warm water for 10 minutes.

2. Drain and chop coarsely.

3. Peel the pear.

4. Remove the core.

5. Chop finely.

6. Finely chop the roast beef.

7. Crumble the amaretti.

8. Combine the sausage meat, breadcrumbs, pear, roast beef, Grana, eggs, raisins, and amaretti in a large bowl.

9. Add the garlic, parsley, lemon zest, nutmeg, cinnamon, pepper, and salt.

10. Mix thoroughly into a soft but dry filling.

11. Cover and refrigerate.

12. Mix the all-purpose flour and semolina.

13. Add the salt.

14. Make a well.

15. Add the 3 eggs.

16. Gradually add about 1 1/4 cups water.

17. Knead.

18. Add the remaining water only if needed to create a smooth elastic dough.

19. Knead for 10–12 minutes.

20. Cover.

21. Rest for 30 minutes.

22. Roll the pasta thin, about 1/32–1/16 inch.

23. Cut disks 2 1/2–3 inches wide.

24. Put about 1 heaping teaspoon filling in the center.

25. Fold into a half-moon.

26. Seal the edges firmly.

27. Press the center of the fold to create the traditional shape.

28. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.

29. Cook for 3–5 minutes.

30. Drain gently.

Service

Dress with melted butter, sage, crisp pancetta, and additional Grana Padano.

Chef's note

The filling should remain soft but not wet; add the measured breadcrumbs gradually if the pear or meats release substantial moisture.

Bigoli Dough

Thick, rough Veneto egg pasta traditionally extruded through a bigolaro press.

Yield: 4–6 servings

Ingredients

3 1/3 cups type 0 or all-purpose flour
4 large eggs
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp extra-virgin olive oil
2/3 tsp fine salt
1/4 cup flour for dusting

Preparation

1. Sift the flour onto a work surface.

2. Make a well.

3. Crack the eggs into the center.

4. Add the salt and olive oil.

5. Beat with a fork while gradually drawing in the flour.

6. Knead by hand for 10–12 minutes.

7. Continue until smooth, elastic, and fairly firm.

8. Cover.

9. Rest for 30 minutes.

10. Divide into pieces sized for the pasta press.

11. Put one piece at a time into a bigolaro or pasta press fitted with a wide die.

12. Extrude long thick strands.

13. Cut to the desired length.

14. Arrange on floured trays.

15. Dry for 20–30 minutes.

16. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.

17. Cook for 6–8 minutes, tasting after 6 minutes.

18. Drain when cooked but still pleasantly chewy.

Service

Dress with duck sauce, anchovy-and-onion sauce, or another Veneto condiment.

Chef's note

The dough should be firmer than tagliatelle dough so the press creates clearly defined rough strands.

24. Meanwhile, melt the butter.

25. Add the poppy seeds.

Carnia stuffed pasta made with a potato dough and a sweet-spiced filling of ricotta, raisins, candied citrus, and cocoa.

Yield: 8 cornetti

Ingredients

3 1/3 cups bread flour
1/3 cup granulated sugar
1/3 cup water
1/3 cup whole milk
about 1 tbsp fresh yeast
1 tsp vanilla extract
1 large egg
3 tbsp softened butter
1 rectangular sheet puff pastry
1/2 tsp fine salt

For brushing
1 large egg
1 tbsp whole milk

Preparation

1. Put the flour, sugar, yeast, vanilla, milk, and water in a mixer bowl.

2. Mix for 2–3 minutes.

3. Add the egg.

4. Knead until absorbed.

5. Add the salt.

6. Gradually work in the softened butter.

7. Continue kneading for about 10 minutes, until smooth and elastic.

8. Cover.

9. Let rise for about 2 hours, until doubled.

10. Roll the brioche dough into a rectangle the same size as the puff pastry.

11. Lay the puff pastry on top.

12. Roll very lightly so the two layers adhere without being compressed.

13. Cut into 8 long triangles.

14. Roll each triangle from the base toward the point.

15. Arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet with the points underneath.

16. Cover.

17. Proof for 45–60 minutes.

18. Preheat the oven to 340°F.

19. Beat the egg with the milk.

20. Brush gently.

21. Bake for about 28 minutes, until deeply golden.

22. Cool on a rack.

Service

Serve warm or at room temperature.

Chef's note

Use very light pressure when rolling the brioche and puff pastry together so both textures remain distinct.

Breakfast Sfogliatella Frolla Dough

Neapolitan lard shortcrust pastry for breakfast-style sfogliatelle frolle.

Yield: dough for about 16 pastries

Ingredients

8 1/3 cups low-protein all-purpose flour
1 3/4 cups lard
1 3/4 cups granulated sugar
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp water
3/4 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Put the flour and cool but pliable lard in a large bowl.

2. Work quickly until sandy.

3. Dissolve the sugar and salt in the water.

4. Gradually add the liquid to the flour mixture.

5. Mix only until the dough comes together.

6. Do not overwork.

7. Shape into a low rectangle.

8. Wrap very well in plastic.

9. Refrigerate for at least 12 hours, preferably 24.

10. Remove from the refrigerator 15 minutes before using.

11. Divide into portions.

12. Roll each portion about 3/16 inch thick.

13. Cut ovals suitable for the traditional shape or molds.

14. Fill with the intended semolina-and-ricotta filling.

15. Close and seal firmly.

16. Arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

17. Bake according to the filling recipe, generally at 375–400°F until golden.

Service

Serve warm or at room temperature.

Chef's note

The long rest allows the lard and flour to stabilize and produces a more crumbly baked pastry.

Breakfast Sfogliatella Riccia

Neapolitan laminated pastry with lard and a semolina, ricotta, citron, and citrus filling.

Yield: 14–16 pastries

Ingredients

For the pastry
4 cups plus 2 tbsp strong all-purpose flour
2/3 cup plus 2 tsp warm water
2 tsp honey
1 1/3 tsp fine salt
1 1/3 cups softened lard

For the filling
1 1/4 cups well-drained sheep’s-milk ricotta
2/3 cup fine semolina
1 1/2 cups water
1 cup granulated sugar
2 large eggs
1 egg yolk
about 1/3 cup diced candied citron
1 tsp ground cinnamon
1 vial orange-flower water
finely grated zest of 1 orange
1/3 tsp fine salt

For finishing
1 large egg
1/3 cup powdered sugar

Preparation

1. Dissolve the honey and salt in the warm water.

2. Put the flour in a large bowl.

3. Gradually add the water.

4. Knead for 10–12 minutes, until smooth and very elastic.

5. Cover.

6. Rest for 30 minutes.

7. Divide into portions.

8. Roll each portion extremely thin, almost transparent.

9. Brush each sheet with softened lard.

10. Stack or join the sheets in the direction of lamination.

11. Roll very tightly into a compact cylinder.

12. Wrap.

13. Refrigerate for at least 8 hours, preferably overnight.

14. For the filling, bring the water, sugar, and salt to a boil.

15. Slowly add the semolina.

16. Cook for 5–7 minutes, stirring.

17. Cool completely.

18. Add the ricotta, eggs, yolk, citron, cinnamon, orange-flower water, and orange zest.

19. Mix until uniform.

20. Cut the pastry roll into slices 3/8–1/2 inch thick.

21. Use your thumbs to gently push the center of each slice outward into a shell.

22. Put about 2 tablespoons filling inside.

23. Close without compressing the laminated edges.

24. Arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

25. Preheat a conventional oven to 400°F.

26. Beat the egg.

27. Brush lightly.

28. Bake for 20–25 minutes, until deeply golden and crisp.

29. Rest for 5 minutes.

30. Dust with powdered sugar.

Service

Serve warm.

Chef's note

Do not compress the laminated edges while shaping; the layers need room to open in the oven.

Polacca Aversana

Aversa yeast cake filled with pastry cream and sour cherries.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

For the dough
1 1/4 cups bread flour
1 cup type 0 or all-purpose flour
scant 1/2 cup whole milk
1/4 cup plus 1 tbsp granulated sugar
1 large egg
3 1/2 tbsp softened butter
about 1 tbsp fresh yeast
finely grated zest of 1 lemon
1/2 tsp fine salt

For the pastry cream
2 cups plus 2 tbsp whole milk
1/2 vanilla bean
3 egg yolks
1/4 cup plus 1 tbsp granulated sugar
1/3 cup all-purpose flour or cornstarch

For the filling
about 2/3 cup drained sour cherries in syrup

For finishing
1 egg yolk
1 tbsp whole milk
1/4 cup pearl sugar

Preparation

1. Prepare the pastry cream.

2. Heat the milk with the vanilla.

3. In a bowl, beat the egg yolks with the sugar.

4. Add the flour or cornstarch.

5. Gradually whisk in the hot milk.

6. Return to the heat.

7. Cook, stirring, until thick.

8. Transfer to a bowl.

9. Cover directly on the surface.

10. Cool completely.

11. For the dough, mix the two flours.

12. Add the sugar, salt, and lemon zest.

13. Add the yeast, egg, and milk.

14. Knead for 5–6 minutes.

15. Gradually work in the softened butter.

16. Continue kneading until smooth and nonsticky.

17. Cover.

18. Let rise for 2–3 hours, until doubled.

19. Divide the dough in half.

20. Roll into two equal disks.

21. Put the first disk into a 9 1/2-inch pan.

22. Spread the cold pastry cream, leaving a 3/4-inch border.

23. Scatter the sour cherries over the cream.

24. Cover with the second disk.

25. Seal the edges firmly.

26. Cover.

27. Proof for 45–60 minutes.

28. Preheat a conventional oven to 350°F.

29. Mix the egg yolk and milk.

30. Brush the surface.

31. Sprinkle with pearl sugar.

32. Bake for about 30 minutes, until golden.

33. Cool before slicing.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

The pastry cream should be cold and firm before it is enclosed in the yeast dough.

Neapolitan Brioche Braid

Soft milk brioche braid flavored with lemon and vanilla and topped with pearl sugar.

Yield: 8 servings

Ingredients

4 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
2 tbsp granulated sugar
1 cup plus 1 tbsp whole milk
1 large egg
3 tbsp plus 1 tsp extra-virgin olive oil
about 2 tsp fresh yeast
finely grated zest of 1 lemon
1 packet vanilla sugar
2/3 tsp fine salt

For brushing
1 egg yolk
1 tbsp whole milk

For finishing
1/3 cup pearl sugar

Preparation

1. Warm the milk.

2. Dissolve the yeast in it.

3. Put the flour and sugar in a large bowl.

4. Add the egg.

5. Add the olive oil.

6. Add the lemon zest and vanilla.

7. Gradually add the yeast milk.

8. Add the salt.

9. Knead for 10–12 minutes, until smooth and elastic.

10. Shape into a ball.

11. Cover.

12. Let rise until doubled, about 2 hours.

13. Divide the dough into three equal portions.

14. Roll into three long even ropes.

15. Join the top ends.

16. Braid without pulling too tightly.

17. Seal the lower ends.

18. Transfer to a parchment-lined baking sheet.

19. Cover.

20. Proof for 45–60 minutes.

21. Preheat a conventional oven to 350°F.

22. Mix the egg yolk and milk.

23. Brush the braid.

24. Sprinkle with pearl sugar.

25. Bake for about 30 minutes.

26. If the top becomes too dark, loosely cover with foil during the final 10 minutes.

27. Cool on a rack.

Service

Serve warm or at room temperature.

Chef's note

Braid loosely so the three strands have room to expand during the final proof.

Pasticciotto Leccese

Salento butter shortcrust pastries filled with vanilla pastry cream.

Yield: about 12 pastries

Ingredients

For the shortcrust pastry
4 cups plus 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
1 2/3 cups powdered sugar
1 cup plus 2 tbsp butter, room temperature
3 large egg yolks
seeds from 1 vanilla bean
1/2 tsp fine salt

For the pastry cream
2 cups plus 2 tbsp whole milk
2/3 cup granulated sugar
6 egg yolks
1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp all-purpose flour
seeds from 1 vanilla bean

Optional filling
12 well-drained sour cherries in syrup

For the molds
1 1/2 tbsp butter
2 tbsp flour

Preparation

1. Mix the flour and butter until sandy.

2. Add the egg yolks.

3. Add the powdered sugar, vanilla, and salt.

4. Work quickly until the pastry is uniform.

5. Shape into a low disk.

6. Wrap in plastic.

7. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes; chill for 1 hour in a warm kitchen.

8. For the pastry cream, heat the milk with the vanilla until almost boiling.

9. Beat the egg yolks with the sugar.

10. Mix in the sifted flour.

11. Gradually whisk in the hot milk.

12. Return everything to the saucepan.

13. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until thick.

14. Transfer to a bowl.

15. Cover directly on the surface.

16. Cool completely.

17. Preheat a conventional oven to 425°F.

18. Butter and flour the pasticciotto molds.

19. Roll the pastry about 3/16 inch thick.

20. Line the bottoms and sides of the molds.

21. Fill each with 2–3 tablespoons pastry cream.

22. Add one sour cherry if using.

23. Cover with a thinner pastry disk.

24. Seal the edges firmly.

25. Bake for 10–12 minutes, until deeply golden.

26. Cool for 2–3 minutes.

27. Unmold carefully.

Service

Serve warm or at room temperature.

Chef's note

The pastry cream must be completely cold before filling so the crust stays clean and crumbly.
